description: A student is getting a 'ModuleNotFoundError' and 'Version Conflict' in their Python environment. They need to fix their virtual environment and dependency tree.

user_profile.context: Trying to run a GitHub repo for a project
user_profile.communication_style: Technical but needs guidance on best practices

fact_sheet.fact: The student encountering the error is Alex Chen, a 21-year-old data science major at Northwood University.
The project is titled 'Project Quasar' for the course CS410: Applied Machine Learning.
Alex is working on a MacBook Pro running macOS Ventura 13.5.
The project's virtual environment, named 'quasar-env', was created with Python 3.11.4.
When running the primary script `main.py`, the terminal displays the error: `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'geoplotter'`.
During the `pip install` process, a version conflict error was logged for the 'scikit-learn' package.
The project was cloned from the GitHub repository at https://github.com/CS410-NU/project-quasar.
The project's `requirements.txt` file specifies `datavizpro==1.5.2`.
The `datavizpro==1.5.2` package has a strict dependency on `scikit-learn==1.2.1`.
The `requirements.txt` file also lists `statmodels-plus==0.8.1`.
The `statmodels-plus==0.8.1` package requires a version of `scikit-learn` that is less than 1.2.0 (`scikit-learn<1.2.0`).
Alex's initial attempt to resolve the issue involved running `pip install --force-reinstall -r requirements.txt`.
Running `pip freeze` inside 'quasar-env' reveals that `scikit-learn` was installed at version 1.1.3.
The output of `pip freeze` also shows that the `datavizpro` and `geoplotter` packages are not installed in the environment.
The teaching assistant for CS410 is Ben Carter.
Ben Carter's office hours are held on Tuesdays from 2:00 PM to 4:00 PM in the Turing Lab, room 303.
Alex Chen's student ID is 901255.
The final submission for Project Quasar is due on November 25, 2023, at 11:59 PM.
The course professor, Dr. Eva Rostova, can be contacted for non-technical questions.
Ben Carter advised Alex to first completely remove the existing virtual environment with the command `rm -rf quasar-env`.
The recommended best practice was to create a new virtual environment using `python3.11 -m venv venv`.
Ben suggested using `pip-tools` to resolve the dependency tree conflicts before installation.
A new file, `requirements.in`, was created containing only the top-level, direct dependencies of the project.
Alex installed `pip-tools` in the new environment using `pip install pip-tools`.
The command `pip-compile requirements.in` was run to generate a new, fully-pinned `requirements.txt` file.
The original installation failed on November 17, 2023.
The newly generated `requirements.txt` resolved the conflict by pinning `scikit-learn==1.1.3` and an older compatible version of `datavizpro`, `datavizpro==1.4.9`.
Alex successfully installed all dependencies from the new file using `pip install -r requirements.txt`.
On November 18, 2023, the command `python main.py` executed without any 'ModuleNotFoundError' or 'Version Conflict' errors.
